## The federal rule for boat registration numbers (33 CFR 173.27)

A registration number must be painted on or permanently attached to **each side of the
forward half** of the vessel; be in **plain vertical block characters of not less than
3 inches in height**; **contrast with the colour of the background** and be distinctly
visible and legible; have **spaces or hyphens** between the letter and number groupings
equal to the width of a letter other than "I" or a number other than "1" (so "TX 1234
AB", not "TX1234AB"); and **read from left to right**.

This rule is federal and applies in every state. States may add requirements but cannot
fall below it. What genuinely varies by state is the number prefix, the issuing agency,
and exactly where the validation decal is placed.

Two common points of confusion:
- **California** uses the prefix **CF**, not CA, and these are locally called "CF numbers".
  **Washington** uses **WN**, not WA.
- A **Hull Identification Number (HIN)** is not a registration number. The HIN is a
  permanent 12-character code stamped into the hull by the builder. The registration
  number is issued by your state and is the one displayed in 3-inch characters.

## USCG documented vessels

A documented vessel does **not** display state registration numbers on the bow. It
displays its **name and hailing port** in characters not less than **4 inches** high on
a clearly visible exterior part of the hull, with the hailing port including both a place
and a state.

- [Boat lettering](https://boatnumbershop.com/boat-lettering/): $29 to start - Boat names, transom text and custom lettering. You pick the font and the colour, we cut it and pre-space it.

- [How to Apply Boat Lettering (Wet and Dry Method)](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/how-to-apply-boat-lettering/): Step-by-step: how to apply pre-spaced boat lettering and registration numbers using the wet method, with the mistakes that ruin a set.
- [How to Remove Old Boat Lettering Without Wrecking Gelcoat](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/how-to-remove-boat-lettering/): Heat, a plastic razor and adhesive remover will lift old boat lettering. What not to use on gelcoat, and how to deal with the shadow left behind.
- [Boat Lettering Fonts: What Works on Water](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/boat-lettering-fonts/): Which fonts read from fifty yards, which ones are legal for registration numbers, and why script fails on a registration number but wins on a transom.
- [Best Vinyl for Boat Lettering: Cast vs Calendared](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/best-vinyl-for-boat-lettering/): Cast vs calendared vinyl for boats, when high-tack is mandatory, and what a film warranty actually covers.
- [Documented Vessel Name & Hailing Port Requirements](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/documented-vessel-name-and-hailing-port/): USCG documented vessels carry the name and hailing port in 4-inch characters, and do not display state registration numbers. Here is the layout.
- [What Boat Registration Numbers Cost in 2026](https://boatnumbershop.com/guides/boat-registration-number-cost/): Boat registration number decals run $10-25 a pair online. What drives the price, what the cheap sets leave out, and what we charge.
